title: Residency-aware RTBF orchestration and evidence streaming
creator: Aisha Gomez
description:
Problem: Customers in regulated regions require automated right-to-be-forgotten (RTBF) workflows that respect data residency and retention policies, provide verifiable proof of deletion, and integrate into their evidence and reporting systems. Current deletion tooling is manual or siloed per-storage type, lacks cross-region orchestration, and does not produce machine-verifiable artifacts for audits.

Goal: Deliver a residency-aware RTBF orchestration feature that: (1) evaluates and applies per-customer retention and residency rules, (2) executes automated deletion pipelines across storage backends and regions, (3) generates tamper-evident deletion receipts and aggregated audit reports, and (4) provides webhook/export hooks to stream evidence into customer SIEM/GRC systems or Redwood Console. The solution must include dry-run and canary verification modes, SLOs for verification success, and clear operator tooling for failed deletions and retries.
acceptance_criteria: Admin UI or API to create per-customer retention policy with residency constraints (region list, min/max retention, resource types)
RTBF job orchestration that locates all data artifacts tied to a subject (tokens, input blobs, embeddings, logs) across regions and storage backends and schedules deletion tasks
Generation of a signed, timestamped deletion receipt per artifact including deletion method, storage backend, deletion hash, and operator id
Ability to stream deletion evidence in near-real-time to a configured customer webhook or S3 bucket in a region matching residency constraints
Verification pipeline that samples deletions and performs independent checks (e.g., HEAD/read tests, hash verification) and reports verification result within 24 hours
Dry-run mode that produces expected deletion plan and evidence without modifying customer data
Console dashboard showing RTBF job status, verification success rate, per-customer audit log export, and error drilldowns
Operational runbook and automated alerting for common failure modes (cross-region replication lag, KMS access denied, transient storage errors)
Automated retention enforcement that blocks new data retention exceeding policy and surfaces conflicts during policy changes
out_of_scope: Full replacement of long-term archival deletion (separate archival purge flows are tracked in ENG-2088)
Client-side consent UIs or customer data discovery outside Redwood-managed artifacts
Legal/subject-access request workflow orchestration beyond providing deletion evidence (legal templates are not part of this ticket)
success_metrics: 90% of RTBF requests complete deletion orchestration and evidence generation within SLA (48 hours)
Verification pipeline reports >= 95% success for sampled deletions after 30 days of operation
Reduction of manual compliance ops time by 70% for customers using automated RTBF
Number of customers enabling residency-aware RTBF >= 10 within quarter after launch
tasks: PM: Finalize PRD and edge case matrix with Legal and Security (deliverable: PRD-v1)
Design: UX flows for policy creation, RTBF request intake, and evidence streaming configuration (links in 'links')
Eng-Infra: Implement residency-aware data locator service (indexing map across regions/backends)
Eng-Storage: Build deletion workers for S3/GCS/DBs with idempotent semantics and signed receipts
Eng-Security: Define signing format for deletion receipts and integrate with KMS/HSM
Eng-Platform: Orchestration service for job scheduling, retry logic, and canary verification
Eng-Console: Dashboard and downloadable audit bundles (machine-readable JSON/NDJSON)
QA: Integration tests covering dry-run, canary, full deletion, and failure scenarios
SRE: SLA/alerting and runbook verification during staged rollout
Docs: API docs for RTBF endpoint and guides for configuring evidence streaming
notes_and_updates: 2025-02-20: Scoping sync with Legal. Confirmed deletion receipts acceptable for EU DPA audits if signed with customer-specific KMS key. Action: involve Security for key policy mapping.
2025-02-24: Spike results - residency-aware locator can index 10M artifacts in ~18 minutes; will need incremental indexing for large tenants. ENG-2011 to own incremental design.
2025-02-28: UX review - PM and Design aligned on a single 'Retention & Residency' policy screen with advanced options collapsed by default. Draft mockups linked.

2025-03-01: Dependencies identified - must wait for ENG-2040 (KMS multi-tenant key access) to enable per-customer signed receipts. Contingency: use Redwood-signed receipts and flag as 'operator-signed' if per-customer keys not yet available.
